correctness.rationale: A direct exact Jacobian identity yields a periodic Poisson kernel; its absolutely convergent Fourier expansion and n-node aliasing give the mass formula. Odd-n strict monotonicity and endpoint limits give uniqueness. For n=2m, an explicitly factored second derivative with a convex exponential chord inequality proves strict log-scale convexity. The equal-weight two-scale even minimizer is fixed by symmetry, and the odd displacement by a uniform near-root expansion. All 277 standalone symbolic/high-precision tests passed. Infinite claims use the displayed proofs; finite tests are corroborative.

value.rationale: The motivating Möbius quadrature assumes fast-decaying weights and zero mapped endpoint; Cauchy mixtures are natural heavy-tailed probability densities with a finite nonzero mapped endpoint. The sharp all-mixture parity dichotomy determines whether changing the Möbius scale can preserve total probability without ex-post renormalization. Strict convexity gives uniqueness of the best even-node scale, and the explicit two-width bias quantifies its unavoidable loss. No claim is made for arbitrary observables or the superiority of scale choice to weight renormalization.
